text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment of this 8-month-old boy, I need to understand his growth trajectory and feeding history. Has he failed to thrive or had significant weight loss, and does he exhibit any specific reactions like arching his back or vomiting after feeds?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby had any recent fevers, changes in stool consistency, or visible blood in the stool? I also need to know if his abdominal distension is constant or if it comes and goes, and whether he passes flatus or stool regularly.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass stool regularly, and if so, is it normal in consistency or does it appear ribbon-like or particularly foul-smelling? I also need to know if there is any family history of thyroid disorders or congenital anomalies.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, and irregular stool passage, I need to rule out a mechanical obstruction or Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction. Barium Enema: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging findings of a transition zone and distal aganglionism are classic for Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
